name: PHP2Shell
summary: Two remote code execution bugs in the PHP runtime, affecting PHP 5.4 and newer on every SAPI (mod_php highest risk, FPM, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed, php-cgi). Leaked Oct 20, patched Oct 21 2026, exploited in the wild.

detail.patched: Version at or above fix. Only patching fixes this one; config changes do not.
detail.default: Only updating PHP fixes this. No setting fully mitigates it.

cves.title: RCE via stale global state (CVSS v4 9.2)

detail.default: Updating is the only complete fix. Turning off session upload progress blocks the confirmed session paths but not other variants.

verdictText.patched: PHP {version} is at or above the fixed release ({fixed}).
verdictText.vulnerable: PHP {version} is below the fixed release {fixed}.
verdictText.noFix: PHP {branch} is end-of-life upstream: no official release fixes it. It is exposed unless the host backported the patch.
verdictText.newer: PHP {version} is newer than any branch in the advisory. Verify manually.
verdictText.older: PHP {version} predates the {minBranch} floor in the advisory but is long dead. Treat as unsafe and verify.

vulnerable.title: Action needed: PHP is not patched for PHP2Shell
vulnerable.sub: This site discloses a PHP version below the fixed release. Update the PHP runtime, then restart.

unknown.title: Cannot confirm: version is hidden
unknown.sub: The site looks like PHP but does not reveal its version. Check the server directly.

patched.title: PHP2Shell: version looks patched
patched.sub: The disclosed version is at or above the fixed release. One setting still needs attention for CVE-2026-115560.

patch.text: Update PHP {branch} from {version} to {fixed} or newer.
PHP {branch} gets no upstream fix. Move to a supported branch (8.5.12, 8.4.27 or 8.3.36 and up), or confirm the host has backported the fix (source backports exist for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1).
Update the PHP runtime itself. Updating WordPress, Laravel or any app does not update PHP; it comes from the server package, the host panel, or the container image.
Restart Apache, PHP-FPM and any long-running PHP workers after updating.
PHP 8.2 reaches end of life on Dec 31, 2026. Plan a move to 8.3 or newer.
Confirm the PHP version that serves web requests: run php -v and php-fpm -v, check the hosting panel, or run local-audit.js on the server.
Required minimums: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Anything on 8.1 or older needs an upgrade or a confirmed vendor backport.
On Debian, Ubuntu or RHEL builds, check the package changelog for CVE-2026-109618; vendors backport fixes under old version numbers.
If patched, still confirm Apache and PHP-FPM were restarted afterward.
Nothing to patch for PHP2Shell based on the disclosed version. Confirm Apache and PHP-FPM were restarted after the update, since old workers keep running old code.
After updating, review memory_limit and post_max_size: the fix adds a hard memory limit that ends the process and skips shutdown handlers.

turnOff.text: Until you can update (reduces exposure, does NOT fix): set memory_limit=-1 so apps cannot override it, keep post_max_size low, and enforce request-size limits at the web server or proxy. Do not use RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA.
On PHP 8.5 also set fatal_error_backtraces=0 until updated.

covered.text: PHP version the site discloses in response headers, compared with the fixed releases ({fixedList})

notCovered.text: Whether workers were restarted after patching

localAudit.vulnerable: PHP {version} < {fixed}: VULNERABLE to PHP2Shell. Update the runtime and restart Apache/PHP-FPM/workers. If this is a distro package, check its changelog for CVE-2026-109618 first; vendors backport under old version numbers.
localAudit.noFix: PHP {branch} is end-of-life upstream with no official fix. Vulnerable unless the vendor backported (source backports exist for 7.4, 8.0, 8.1). Check the package changelog for CVE-2026-109618, or upgrade.
